Rationale: it is the browser counterpart of opentelemetry-instrumentation / distributed-tracing-design / structured-logging-design, all of which are domain=observability despite owner=backend-engineer — instrumentation subject already overrides owner elsewhere in the taxonomy, and grouping the only react-* telemetry skill under frontend would split the observability capability across two domains in the P3 derived catalog. This is the sole deviation from the prefix/suffix rule across all 186 skills (audited at close-out); the rule text above is updated to match reality rather than leaving the deviation silent. Revisit at P3 if the catalog's capability view prefers strict prefixing.

p4_complete.rescope: The charter estimated P4 at ~120–186 children — 'one child per skill flagged by the P1 duplication linter', deleting each restatement and repointing it. Auditing the actual backlog BEFORE generating any issues showed it was ~99% false positives, so P4 was rescoped to 8 children that fixed the detector rather than mutilating compliant skills.
why_the_backlog_was_false: All 13 recurring-block clusters (62 skills) were the MANDATED artifact frontmatter (name/version/phase/owner/created) inside each skill's `## Output Format` template. CLAUDE.md § Artifact Standards REQUIRES that block, so its recurrence is compliance, not duplication — deleting or repointing it would violate the standard the linter exists to enforce. Verified mechanically: 62/62 flagged blocks sat inside a `---` + `name:` template.

5 of the 7 CLAUDE.md 'restatements' were also false positives: python-contract-test CITES CLAUDE.md with attribution (the correct behaviour); opentofu-module's flagged string was a Terraform tenant_id regex, not CLAUDE.md's component-naming regex; sdlc-config-management legitimately constrains product_slug and explains why; glossary-management is the allow-listed HOME for glossary definitions; integration-design merely USES canonical glossary terms, which CLAUDE.md § Ubiquitous Language mandates.
p4_complete.why_fix_the_detector_rather_than_declare: A report where 60+ of 62 findings are noise is worse than no report: a genuine future duplication would hide among the false positives and the P4 backlog would read as permanently unfinished. Charter decision #5 makes the consistency linter the campaign keystone — a keystone with this precision is not doing its job.

delivered_children: #1209 — product-strategist: the LIGHT first child (manifest fields only; the agent was already v2.0.0 with a Behavioral Directives index and a passing acceptance test). It ESTABLISHED the produces/domain/status convention every later agent child follows, and reported that nothing yet consumed the fields.

#1211 — wire agent produces/domain/status through manifest.py -> lint-manifests.py -> build-catalog.py. The fields child 1 authored reached NOTHING: load_agents() never read them, record_to_instance() projected a hard-coded 12-field tuple so they never reached the validator, and _agent_entry() emitted no such key. PROVEN, not inferred — injecting a typo'd 'domainn:' still produced 'TOTAL 0 violation(s) / RESULT: PASS', i.e. additionalProperties:false was NOT actually enforced on agents. Root cause fixed at source: all three loaders now capture unrecognised authored keys into an 'extra' dict, and lint-manifests SUBTRACTS a closed set of derived keys instead of enumerating an allow-list, so the NEXT manifest field is enforced the day manifest.py reads it. Catalog 'artifacts' values became kind-tagged {agents:[], skills:[]} (a flat list is genuinely undecidable when a skill and an artifact share a name). Tests 48->58, 24->31, 41->66.

#1213 — backend-engineer, full refactor, v1.1.0 -> 2.0.0. THE EXEMPLAR: trigger-surface description, product-strategist body shape, 8 Behavioral Directives, 22 produces entries, stated test-strategist and security-engineer boundaries. 1 directive-citation defect found and fixed (directive 1.3 cited sync.Pool to go-concurrency-patterns, where it appears nowhere; the substance is genuinely in go-performance-optimization and was already cited correctly elsewhere, so the citation was RE-POINTED rather than the content duplicated).

#1215 — frontend-engineer, full refactor, v2.1.0 -> 3.0.0. 16 produces entries; ux-architect and test-strategist boundaries resolved in the file (specs are INPUTS; TDD means the implementing agent writes its own component/e2e tests); dockerfile claimed PER-INSTANCE alongside backend-engineer's Go image. 6 citation defects fixed — each asserted substance absent from the cited skill ('design-system' in react-component-design, 'aggregation gateway' in react-observability, 'npm run ci' in react-project-structure, 'numeric non-root UID' in react-dockerfile, 'Gherkin' in react-e2e-testing, 'packages/api-client' in react-api-client) and each was re-pointed to the skill that actually holds it, never duplicated.

#1217 — platform-engineer, full refactor, v1.1.0 -> 2.0.0, plus the campaign's FIRST NEWLY-WRITTEN acceptance test. 18 produces entries; image/health, security and data-pipeline seams stated explicitly. ZERO mis-pointed citations. One real defect: the inherited refactor had COMPRESSED the old Operator-pattern directive down to a bullet, DELETING substance instead of relocating it — restored as 'The Operator Ladder' in skills/kubernetes-workload-patterns/references/controller-decision-table.md (1.0.0 -> 1.1.0), with the agent citing it and rung 3 made an ADR-plus-approval escalation. The test prompt was also DE-LEAKED: as inherited it named the default-deny NetworkPolicy it then asserted on, so a pass proved nothing; rewritten to ask what the skill's standard requires, and it still passes — which is the actual evidence that the answer was skill-derived.
binding_conventions: description IS THE TRIGGER SURFACE, not a bio. Enumerate the literal verbs, deliverable names and symptom phrasings a matching request would contain ('the service is slow', 'the pod is CrashLooping', 'the bundle is too big'). Rewriting it forces a MAJOR version bump on its own (CLAUDE.md two-surface rule).

produces ORDER MIRRORS the prose outputs: list exactly, so a PM can diff the two line-for-line without tooling. Verify programmatically (produces == [first token of each outputs entry]), not by eye. Alphabetical order is NOT used — the catalog sorts on read anyway.
EVERY produces name must already be a key in generated/catalog.json -> artifacts. Never invent one. An artifact no skill produces is a FINDING to report, not a name to add.
CANDIDATES come from the union of the agent's skills' produces:; the AUTHORITY is the agent's own § Responsibilities 'Owns' line. An agent does not produce everything its skills can produce.

EXCLUDE the three cross-cutting artifacts: ubiquitous-language-glossary (glossary-management), methodology-compliance-report (methodology-review) and handoff-record (ddd-agent-handoff). 11 of 13 agents carry ddd-agent-handoff, so claiming handoff-record would make 'who produces this artifact?' meaningless. State the exclusion in the file under 'Applied but not owned'.

STACK-NEUTRAL artifacts (dockerfile, makefile, schema-migration, load-test-suite, mutation-report, performance-regression-gate) are claimed PER-INSTANCE, not exclusively — backend-engineer claims the Go image, frontend-engineer the React one. The catalog's artifacts map holds a LIST of producers precisely so this works. Only SAME-STACK duplicate claims are overlap defects. Write the reasoning into § Responsibilities so it is inherited, not re-litigated.

VERIFY EVERY BEHAVIORAL DIRECTIVE AGAINST THE CITED SKILL'S CONTENT — open the skill and grep for the actual claim; confirming the skill EXISTS is not the check. This found 7 real defects across children 3-5. Per CLAUDE.md, a directive whose substance is absent from the cited skill is a DEFECT: re-point the citation to the skill that holds it, or move the substance INTO a skill. Never duplicate content between skills — that manufactures exactly the restatement lint-duplication exists to catch.

ACCEPTANCE-TEST PROMPTS MUST NOT LEAK THEIR OWN ANSWERS. #1217 tightened an inherited prompt that named the default-deny NetworkPolicy it was about to assert on; a pass would have proved nothing. Ask for 'what the skill's standard requires' and let the agent derive it. An acceptance test checks what the agent PRODUCED, not what it can recite.
capability: is DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED on any agent (charter decision #2 — a derived view over the relationship graph, never a hand-authored tier).

Body shape follows product-strategist / backend-engineer: Purpose, Responsibilities (Owns / Does not own), Behavioral Directives, Execution Sequence, Decision Process, Methodology Application, Escalation Rules, Completion Criteria. inputs/outputs are artifact names with a parenthetical gloss, not prose blobs.
Rebuild and COMMIT generated/catalog.json in any child that changes agent frontmatter — step 5 of the gate is blocking on staleness.

Tightening them to mirror skill.schema.json breaks an existing assertion in tests/schemas/agent.schema.test.py that accepts status: 'active' (outside the skill enum experimental|stable|complete). project.name: SDLC Artifact Factory
project.author: Shafi Babar
project.description: A Claude Code plugin that takes a problem statement and drives a product through its full SDLC lifecycle — Strategy → Ideate → Design → Implement → Data → Quality → Deploy → Customer Validation — producing real, reviewable, methodology-compliant artifacts at every phase.

working_agreements.operator: Shafi Babar. Product Manager. Solo operator (Han Solo). Not a programmer. Provides problem statements, reviews artifacts, approves each chunk before proceeding.
working_agreements.claude_role: Principal engineer. Does all implementation — skills, agents, commands, hooks, tools, code generation. Shafi approves; Claude builds.
working_agreements.session_startup: Read sdlc-context.json first. Restore context from this file, not from conversation history.
working_agreements.chunk_gate: After Chunk 4: each subsequent chunk is planned, discussed, and explicitly approved by Shafi before execution. No chunk starts without a go.
working_agreements.build_discipline: One chunk at a time. One commit per chunk. Nothing in a later chunk is started while an earlier chunk is incomplete.
working_agreements.budget_posture: Frugal. Open-source preferred. No paid APIs, no expensive tooling. Process and methodology are the investment, not tooling.
working_agreements.timeline: Iterative. No deadlines. Quality over speed.

non_negotiables: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) — Ubiquitous Language, Bounded Contexts, Domain Events, Aggregates
Event Storming — applied at Design phase for every domain and subdomain
Test-Driven Development (TDD) — tests written before implementation code, always
Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) — Gherkin feature files for all acceptance criteria
SOLID — applied across all generated code artifacts
methodology.enforcement: Absence of an applicable methodology in any artifact is a defect, not a warning. Phase gate hooks enforce compliance before advancing.

tech_stack._note: These are the default target-stack decisions. Parameterized per product at /sdlc-start time. Saved to sdlc-config.json per product.

confirmed.api_framework: net/http + chi — idiomatic, lightweight, no magic, code-reviewable. Chosen over Gin/Echo/Fiber for compliance-grade transparency.
confirmed.primary_database: PostgreSQL + pgx — ACID, audit log, config store, outbox table. Default for all services.
confirmed.search_and_alerts: Elasticsearch — document indexing, full-text search, alert storage.
confirmed.message_broker: Redpanda — Kafka-API compatible, no JVM, frugal, familiar Kafka tooling.
confirmed.graph_database: Apache AGE (default, PostgreSQL extension, zero extra infra). Neo4j Community as selectable alternative when graph is primary product surface.
confirmed.ci_cd: GitHub Actions — native to GitHub repos, free tier, zero hosting overhead.
confirmed.iac: OpenTofu (infrastructure provisioning, open-source Terraform fork) + Helm (application deployment onto Kubernetes).
confirmed.service_mesh: Linkerd — Rust data plane, automatic mTLS, lowest resource overhead, CNCF graduated.
confirmed.container_orchestration: Kubernetes. EKS/AKS/GKE via OpenTofu for customer cloud. k3s for managed private tenants. kind for local development. Single Helm chart per service, environment differences in values.yaml.
confirmed.observability: OpenTelemetry (Go SDK) + Prometheus (metrics) + Elasticsearch + Fluent Bit (logs) + Tempo (traces) + Grafana (single pane). Kibana optional for deep log analysis.
confirmed.optional_database: MongoDB — variable-schema bounded contexts (entity extraction output, crawl metadata). Exposed as config option at /sdlc-start. Not default.

tech_stack.sdlc_start_questionnaire: Interactive questionnaire at /sdlc-start saves answers to sdlc-config.json per product. Allows per-product overrides of defaults above.

first_product.name: Data Estate Mapping and Compliance Intelligence
first_product.core_value: Maps an organisation's data estate across storage systems, extracts entities, builds a relationship graph, and provides compliance intelligence — with zero data ever leaving customer infrastructure.
first_product.architecture_style: Event-driven microservices with physical tenant isolation
first_product.pipeline: Worker nodes at customer storage → Message Queue → File Processing → Entity Extraction → Graph Update → Compliance Rule Engine → Alert + Audit
first_product.deployment_model: Option A: one-click deploy to customer's own AWS/Azure/GCP. Option B: managed private cloud with dedicated tenant, no data commingling.
first_product.security: Zero Trust, OAuth 2.0 + JWT, mTLS via Linkerd, ABAC claim-based authorization, API-First (UI is first-party API consumer only)
first_product.test_strategy: TDD as default. Test layers: Unit, Integration, Contract, E2E, Extraction quality, Security.
first_product.status: Not yet started — plugin must be built first.

plugin_architecture.description: Commands drive phases. Phases activate agents. Agents draw on skills for expertise and scripts (via Bash) for atomic actions. Hooks enforce governance automatically, calling scripts or consulting skills directly. Artifacts are outputs of the workflow, not the inputs.
plugin_architecture.component_hierarchy: Command → Agent → Skill | Agent → Script (via Bash) | Hook → Script or → Agent/Skill

axioms.Skills: Expertise — domain knowledge, standards, patterns. No reasoning.
axioms.Agents: Reasoning — decisions, analysis, design, code generation. Use skills for knowledge.
axioms.Commands: Workflows — user-facing phase drivers and cross-cutting operations.
axioms.Hooks: Governance — event-driven, lightweight, fast, idempotent. No business logic.
axioms.Scripts: Atomic actions — deterministic, stateless, single-purpose. Not a Claude Code discovery mechanism; 'Tools' means MCP-exposed tools specifically.
